content.summary: Implementation plan for: Git Review UI with live project git state, file sidebar, diff viewing, and line commenting

data.goal: Add a /changes route to the TUI that shows live staged+unstaged git changes with file navigation, adaptive diff rendering, and buffered line comments that submit into the prompt.
data.learning_milestone: A user can type /changes, navigate files, see diffs, add a comment to a line, press S, and see the formatted comment appear in their chat prompt ready to send. If this flow works end-to-end, the architecture is validated.
data.approach:
We add a new route type ('changes') to the existing SolidJS routing system, create a new route folder at routes/changes/ containing 4-5 components (index, file-list, diff-pane, footer, format-comments), and enrich the existing File.status() server endpoint to distinguish staged vs unstaged changes.

The diff rendering reuses the existing <diff> opentui element already used throughout the session route — no new rendering primitives needed. The file list fetches data from the SDK client, which talks to the enriched /file/status endpoint.

Line commenting is stored in a local createStore (in-memory, not persisted) and formatted into a structured text block on submit. Submit navigates back to home/session with the formatted comments as initialPrompt, leveraging the existing PromptInfo pattern.

This approach keeps all new code under routes/changes/ (4 new files) with minimal touches to existing files (route.tsx, app.tsx, file/index.ts, server/routes/file.ts). This minimizes fork conflicts with upstream.

changes_required.change: Add optional 'stage' field to File.Info schema; split File.status() into staged+unstaged git commands
No code changes needed — schema change propagates automatically
Add ChangesRoute type to Route union
Add <Match> for 'changes' route; register /changes slash command
NEW: Main Changes route component with layout (sidebar + diff pane + footer)
NEW: File list sidebar with staged/unstaged grouping and keyboard navigation
NEW: Diff viewing pane using existing <diff> element
NEW: Footer with summary stats and keybind hints
NEW: Pure function to format comment array into prompt text

technical.why_hard: The <diff> opentui element renders diffs but may not expose which line the user's cursor is on. There's no documented API for line-level interaction callbacks on the diff element.
technical.mitigation: Fallback approach: prompt user for line number when pressing 'c', or comment on the visible hunk. Alternatively, wrap diff lines in individual box elements with click handlers — but this changes the rendering approach significantly. Start with hunk-level or prompted-line commenting for MVP.

technical.challenge: Staged vs unstaged diff content from File.read()
technical.why_hard: The existing File.read() endpoint generates diff by running 'git diff' then falling back to 'git diff --staged'. It doesn't parameterize which diff to show. A staged file might show the wrong diff.
technical.mitigation: For MVP, the combined diff (working tree vs HEAD) is acceptable and matches what most users expect. If needed later, add a 'ref' query parameter to File.read() to specify --cached. Don't block on this.

technical.why_hard: When navigating from session → changes → session, we need to return to the correct session. The current route system doesn't have a history stack.
technical.mitigation: Store returnTo route in ChangesRoute type. On Escape, navigate to returnTo (or home as fallback). Simple and sufficient.

dependencies: SDK regeneration after File.Info schema change (automated via ./script/generate.ts)
Understanding of <diff> opentui element capabilities (may need to inspect opentui source for line interaction APIs)
skills_required: SolidJS reactive patterns (signals, stores, memos, effects)
OpenTUI element model (box, scrollbox, text, diff)
Git CLI commands for staged/unstaged/untracked distinction
Existing opencode TUI patterns (routes, commands, dialogs, themes)
risk_factors: The <diff> element's line interaction capabilities are unknown — may need to explore opentui source
Large diff files could cause performance issues in the scrollbox
Fork conflicts if upstream touches route.tsx or app.tsx between now and merge

open_questions: Does the <diff> opentui element support any form of line-level click/cursor callbacks? If not, what's the simplest way to know which line the user is looking at?
Should the /changes route be accessible from both home and session routes, or only session?
Should comments persist across route changes (e.g., stored in KV) or is in-memory sufficient for MVP?
Should the file list support filtering/searching, or is scroll-based navigation enough for v1?

unit: format-comments.ts: pure function, test with various comment arrays (empty, single, multi-file, special characters)
File.status() enrichment: test that staged, unstaged, and untracked files get correct stage values (requires git repo fixture)
integration: Manual TUI testing: launch opencode, type /changes, verify file list loads, select a file, see diff, press c, type comment, press S, verify prompt is populated
Typecheck: bun run typecheck must pass after all changes
Route roundtrip: navigate home → /changes → Escape → verify returns to home; navigate session → /changes → Escape → verify returns to session

risks.risk: opentui <diff> element has no line interaction API
risks.mitigation: Fall back to hunk-level commenting or line-number prompt dialog. This reduces UX quality but doesn't block the feature.

risks.risk: File.read() diff content doesn't match staged state
risks.mitigation: Accept combined diff for MVP; add --cached parameter support as a fast follow-up.

risks.risk: Upstream changes to route.tsx or app.tsx cause merge conflicts
risks.mitigation: Keep changes to these files minimal (3-5 lines each). The bulk of new code is in routes/changes/ which won't conflict.

risks.risk: Performance with large repos (hundreds of changed files)
risks.mitigation: Use scrollbox with virtualization if opentui supports it; otherwise, cap displayed files at 100 with a 'show all' option.

included_now: New /changes route with file sidebar + diff pane + footer
Adaptive split/unified diff based on terminal width
Keyboard navigation (arrows, enter, escape, c, S)
deferred: File tree grouping by directory (flat list is fine for v1)
Inline diff annotations (slottable-diff style) — explicitly out of scope per requirements
Staged-specific diff viewing (--cached parameter on File.read())
Auto-refresh on file system changes (manual refresh via keybind is sufficient)
